newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major denies plans to impose VAT on food.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major denies plans to impose VAT on food.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major and his finance minister Kenneth Clarke on Wednesday denied an assertion by the opposition Labour Party that the ruling Conservatives plan to impose Value Added Tax on food.
Labour is running a campign saying VAT on food will be one of the Conservatives' "first targets" if it wins the election, which must be held by May.
After talks with Major, Chancellor of the Exchequer Clarke accused Labour of a "deliberate lie" in claiming family food bills would rise if the Conservatives win a fifth term.
He said: "Neither the prime minister nor I have any intention of imposing VAT on food so long as we are in government.

"This deliberate lie shows Labour will say anything to get elected and do anything to avoid explaining where the money would come from to fund their 30 billion pounds ($50 billion) of spending pledges."

Labour responded by pointing to promises made by the Conservatives before the last general election in 1992 not to increase VAT. Labour says these pledges were broken with the introduction of VAT on various new goods and services.
In its campaign, Labour warns voters that the government cannot be trusted on VAT because it is its "favourite tax" ($1=.5976 Pound)
